problem: Zero-shot foundation-model VLN navigators rely on local visual cues and linear histories, lacking a global spatial state of explored regions, paths and landmarks, so they get lost in multi-space or complex tasks; map-based alternatives need costly pre-exploration.
motivation: VLN-CE needs spatial structure understanding to localize instruction progress, yet VLMs are weak at global spatial reasoning. An online, training-free spatial memory that lets the VLM verify progress and plan verifiable stages could close this gap without pre-built maps or task-specific training.
key_idea: Build an online hierarchical Spatial Cognitive Memory (Spatial Waypoint graph/chain plus subtask-grounded landmark pool) and use a schema-guided Spatial-CoT in a planner-executor stagewise closed loop that emits verifiable space-landmark stages.
insight: Ablations show spatial memory is the dominant contributor: removing Hierarchical Spatial Memory drops R2R-CE SR from 53.3 to 38.9 (removing both memories: 37.3), and removing planner Spatial-CoT costs more (SR 44.8) than executor Spatial-CoT (47.1), showing that planner-side spatial verification and anchor selection matter most. Stagewise control also cuts steps (205.5 to ~171.7) via verification and replanning. Backend models with stronger spatial ability (Qwen3.5) do better.
method: Stagewise closed-loop framework: planner reads task, 12-view look-around and memory, builds a space-landmark anchor chain, localizes the furthest verified anchor and outputs only the next stage subtask (anchor, direction, instruction, landmark, completion flag); executor runs it and returns feedback for verification/replanning.

Hierarchical Spatial Memory: online metric RGB-D map abstracted into Spatial Waypoints (pose, floor, region, landmarks) forming a graph (map reachability + chain adjacency) and executed waypoint chain, serialized into an agent-centered adjacency list plus rendered map.
Local Landmark Memory: subtask-specific ranked top-K landmark pool from GroundingDINO + RepViT-SAM grounding, depth-fused with distance, bearing, confidence, visibility and arrival flags.
Planner Spatial-CoT: five-field schema (observation, memory perception, progress, decision, plan summary) verifying the anchor chain against panorama and spatial context.
Executor Spatial-CoT: four-field schema (view, landmark detection, progress, action) constrained to a locally admissible action set with obstacle cues.
Reliability controls: output validation with bounded retries, action masking on ineffective motion, turn limits (N_turn=3), stage/episode budgets and landmark-grounded stop criteria.

setting.backbone: Qwen3.5-Plus (planner) + Qwen3.5-Flash (executor), frozen; open-source variant Qwen3.5-122B-A10B + Qwen3.5-35B-A3B; GroundingDINO + RepViT-SAM for grounding
setting.model_size: 122B-A10B planner + 35B-A3B executor (open-source variant); Plus/Flash sizes undisclosed
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (640x480, 79° HFOV) + metric pose, 12-view look-around at planning steps
setting.action_space: low-level Stop / MoveForward 0.25 m / TurnLeft 30° / TurnRight 30°
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D for R2R-CE/RxR-CE, HM3D for OVON)
setting.privileged: none (pose given as input; no pre-exploration)

numbers.extra: TX-Q1 robot, 8-view scan, 2 m success radius

numbers_note: Backbone for GN-Bench and OVON rows is not explicitly stated; assumed the main Qwen3.5-Plus/Flash config.
results: SpaceVLN sets new zero-shot SR of 53.3 on R2R-CE (vs GTA 48.8), 48.9 on RxR-CE (vs GTA 46.2), 39.3 on GN-Bench, and 51.6 on HM3D-OVON (vs DRIVE-Nav 50.2). It beats some supervised and pre-exploration methods, but SPL (34.5) trails GTA (41.8) on R2R-CE. Real-robot SR is 48% vs Open-Nav 34%.
limitations: Sensitive to noisy waypoint labels, open-vocabulary grounding errors and dense relative-turn instructions, affecting progress localization and stopping.
No long-horizon geometric planner, so detours and occluded regions require repeated replanning; SPL lags SR.
Many repeated foundation-model calls limit efficiency; dependent on strong VLM backends.
